diagnostic_evidence.quote: $\gL^{h, \lambda} f = h^{-1} \gL(h f) - h^{-1} f \gL h = \gL f + h^{-1} \Gamma(h, f)$

issues.failure_explanation: With the stated definition, the displayed identity is false. The standard carré du champ is $\Gamma(h,f)=\gL(hf)-h\gL f-f\gL h$; the given expression is not equivalent, so the theorem's formula does not hold as written.

failure_location.quote: where $\Gamma(h, f) = h \gL(h^{-1} f) - f \gL h^{-1}$ is the carr\'e du champ operator associated with the generator $\gL$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the definition by the standard carré du champ $\Gamma(h,f)=\gL(hf)-h\gL f-f\gL h$ (and correct the conservative condition to $\gL^{h,\lambda}1=0$).
issues.overall_effect: The generalized Doob transform formula is misstated; downstream use of this theorem as a justification is not supported by the displayed definition.
issues.title: Incorrect carré du champ definition in generalized Doob h-transform
issues.why_classification: The correction is a local standard formula; no substantive result is lost.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: The diffusion matrix $\mD_s(\vx) \in \R^{d \times d}$ is positive definite for any $\vx \in \R^d$
Consider the special case where the diffusion component vanishes, i.e., $\mD_t(\vx) \equiv 0$

issues.failure_explanation: Pure jump processes have $D=0$, which is positive semidefinite but not positive definite. The paper later uses $D=0$ in the α-stable example and the jump model, so the stated theorem excludes its own admissible cases. The correct condition is positive semidefinite.

failure_location.quote: where $\vb_t(\vx)$ is the drift term, $\mD_t(\vx)$ is the diffusion coefficient which positive definite for any $\vx \in \R^d$

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Change 'positive definite' to 'positive semidefinite' in the theorem and regularity assumptions.
issues.overall_effect: The claimed general Lévy-type representation and the pure-jump examples do not satisfy the theorem's hypotheses as stated.
issues.title: Positive definite diffusion matrix excludes pure jump processes
issues.why_classification: One-word local correction; all substantive claims survive.

issues.failure_explanation: The definition of $\gI$ restricts the integral to the unit ball $B(\vx,1)$, whereas the displayed Fourier expression is the principal-value integral over all of $\R^d$. The domain mismatch changes the drift term; the formula is not valid for the defined $\gI$ without an additional outside-ball correction.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Either redefine $\gI$ as the full principal-value integral or add the missing outside-ball contribution to the Fourier formula.
issues.overall_effect: The α-stable backward drift and the practical implementation based on this formula are not justified by the paper's definition.
issues.title: Fourier formula for α-stable integral uses wrong integration domain
issues.why_classification: Requires correcting a nontrivial integral identity, but the example can be repaired without changing the overall framework.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: we set the drift $\vb_t(\vx) \equiv \vzero$ and the diffusion coefficient $\mD_t(\vx) \equiv \vzero$

issues.failure_explanation: With $b=0$ and $D=0$, the general Lévy-type generator still contains the small-jump compensation term $-\int_{B(\vx,1)}(\vy-\vx)\cdot\nabla f(\vx)\lambda_t(\dif\vy,\vx)$. Dropping it is valid only if the first moment of the small jumps vanishes; otherwise the drift must be set to that moment. The assumption $\int_{B}|\vy|\lambda<\infty$ makes the moment finite but does not make it zero.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Either retain the compensation term or include the first moment of the small jumps in the drift.
issues.overall_effect: The derivation of the pure-jump forward process is incorrect for asymmetric kernels; the experiment uses a symmetric kernel, so that special case remains valid.
issues.title: Pure jump generator simplification omits small-jump compensation
issues.why_classification: Local correction; the main experimental case with symmetric kernel is unaffected.

issues.failure_explanation: The integral $\gJ$ is a convolution of $\varphi$ with the kernel centered at $\vy_t^{(k)}$. Replacing the center by a fixed reference changes the kernel location; the equality would require the convolution value to factor as a constant times $\varphi(\vy_t^{(k)})$, which is false for a general score/kernel.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Compute the convolution integral for each sample (e.g., via FFT over all samples) instead of reusing a single reference integral by division.
issues.overall_effect: The claimed computational shortcut for the jump model's backward simulation is invalid; the experimental implementation based on it is not justified.
issues.title: Invalid reuse of jump integral across different centers
issues.why_classification: Invalidates an algorithmic shortcut and may materially increase cost, but the overall jump model can still be implemented correctly.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: where the last equality is by Dynkin's formula

issues.failure_explanation: The correct h-transform Radon-Nikodym derivative must contain the factor $h_t/h_0$ (here $\eta_{T-t}(\cev x_t)/\eta_T(\cev x_0)$) and the time derivative in the exponential. The displayed derivative omits this factor and replaces the pathwise h-transform formula by an expectation-level Dynkin identity; hence it is not a probability measure and does not yield the claimed generator.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the Radon-Nikodym derivative by the correct time-inhomogeneous h-transform formula with the missing $\eta_{T-t}(\cev x_t)/\eta_T(\cev x_0)$ factor and the appropriate time-derivative term, then rederive the KL identity.
issues.overall_effect: The formal change-of-measure theorem and its immediate corollaries are not established as written. The KL formula and error bounds may be recoverable from the corrected derivative, but the source's proof is invalid.
issues.title: Change-of-measure Radon-Nikodym derivative missing h-transform factor
issues.why_classification: Central theorem has a false explicit derivative, but the repair is a standard h-transform correction and the main KL/error results can be preserved.
